name: vault-reader
description: Lightweight Obsidian vault I/O plugin for searching notes, loading domain context, restoring session context, and creating session notes. Use from external projects to access vault knowledge.

hooks.prompt: Check if the user's most recent message contains an explicit session-closing signal: '세션 끝', '세션 마무리', '세션 종료', '오늘은 여기까지', '마무리하자', '그만하자', '끝내자', '오늘 끝', 'wrap up', 'let's end', 'we're done for today', 'end session', 'session done', 'finish up', 'call it a day', 'that's all'. ONLY if such a signal is present, use AskUserQuestion to offer session-note creation: [네, 기록] full session-note via vault-searcher Mode 4, [간단히] quick-mode session-note, [건너뛰기] skip. If NO closing signal is present, do NOTHING — this hook fires every turn, so silent pass-through is the default behavior. Never auto-create a session note without confirmation. Note: /exit and /quit cannot be predicted by this hook (they terminate the session before the next Stop fires); SessionEnd hook handles that case as a safety net.

The session is ending (user exited or timed out). Save a safety-net session-note INLINE (do NOT delegate to vault-searcher Mode 4 — that mode requires AskUserQuestion which cannot fire during session close). Create the file ONLY if the session had meaningful work — defined as 3+ turns AND at least one of: (a) file modification/creation, (b) vault read, (c) explicit decision or recommendation recorded, (d) code execution or test run, (e) external research (WebFetch/docs lookup). Pure Q&A dialogue with no artifacts → skip entirely. Procedure: (1) Resolve target path: start with ~/vault/00_Inbox/session-YYYY-MM-DD.md. Use Bash (`ls ~/vault/00_Inbox/session-YYYY-MM-DD*.md 2>/dev/null`) or Glob to check collision. If base exists, append `-v2`, then `-v3`, incrementing until a free filename is found. (2) Write the file via the Write tool. Frontmatter MUST contain EXACTLY these three fields and no others — do NOT include a `status` field (record-style): `created: YYYY-MM-DD`, `tags: [session, auto-saved]`, `type: session`. (3) Body: a '## Summary' section (2-3 lines recapping the session), then '## Related Files' listing paths touched during the session. No further sections required. (4) Do NOT use AskUserQuestion — the session is closing and cannot accept user input. (5) If Write fails for any reason (permission, path missing), log the failure via a single assistant message and stop; do not retry.
